method: A staff position counts diatonic steps: line 1 is step 0, the space above it step 1, line 2 step 2, with the space below the staff at -1 and ledger lines at -2, -4 and so on below and 10, 12 and up above. Each clef fixes one written letter to one staff line: the G clef marks G4 on its line, the F clef F3 and the C clef C4, so a pitch's position is the reference step plus the diatonic difference and a position's pitch is the reference pitch plus the step difference. Positions cover -6 to 14, three ledger lines below and above the staff; the comparison table runs the same pitch through all nine clefs and marks positions outside that range. An accidental is carried into the written and sounding names but never moves the note, and a clef with an octave change lowers the sounding octave by one, so a written C4 in the tenor-voice treble clef sounds C3. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: W3C MusicXML 4.0, The <clef> element: clefs are represented by a combination of the sign, line and clef-octave-change elements, so a clef names G, F or C and the line places it on the staff.
Wikipedia, Clef: the C clef marks middle C, the G clef G4 and the F clef F3, and the clef is placed on a counted line of the staff.
